when: Week 1, day 3. Type the code yourself; do not copy-paste.

sittings.bodyEn: Five ideas cover reading and writing model code: tensor, shape, autograd, module, and training loop. Type the chapter snippets yourself — do not copy-paste. Most model bugs are shape bugs. Interviewers ask for the five-line training order and for B, T, C shapes. This chapter is the toolbox for Project 2 and Project 5.

terms.hook: If they say this, they mean the array of numbers with a shape.

sittings.bodyEn: A tensor is an array of numbers with a shape. A table [[1,2,3],[4,5,6]] has shape (2, 3); multiply by ones(3,2) and you get (2, 2). Matrix multiply needs matching inner sizes; broadcasting stretches size-1 dims; view keeps the same count of numbers; transpose swaps two dimensions. Print shape on both sides before a multiply when you see mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied. Say shape first when debugging.

terms.hook: If they say this, start with shape, then ops.

sittings.bodyEn: In model code, B is batch size, T is sequence length, and C is channels — vector width. Attention often makes (B, T, T) score matrices. Example: (8, 128, 64) times (8, 64, 128) yields (8, 128, 128). That is the chapter 6 T-by-T idea with an explicit batch dimension. Keep shapes labeled B, T, C when you read attention code.

terms.hook: If they ask attention shapes, label B, T, C on the tensors.

sittings.bodyEn: Mark a tensor with requires_grad True and PyTorch records every operation. Calling backward fills grad with the gradient. For loss equals (3w − 12) squared at w equals 2, the gradient is −36.0. Autograd is why you do not write derivatives by hand for every layer. Interviewers may ask what requires_grad and backward do — answer in one clear sentence each.

terms.hook: If they mix autograd with step size, separate gradient from learning rate.

sittings.bodyEn: Every training step is the same five lines: forward, loss, zero_grad, backward, step. Memorize that order — interviewers ask for it. Forward builds predictions; loss scores them; zero_grad clears old slopes; backward fills new ones; step updates weights. Keep this loop in muscle memory for Project 2 and Project 5. Wrong order is a common oral-exam fail.

terms.hook: If they say this in PyTorch, CrossEntropyLoss wants class ids and raw logits.

sittings.bodyEn: nn.Module is the building block: a layer is a module, and a model contains modules. nn.Sequential chains them. Two linear layers with ReLU between them learn inside versus outside a circle. Remove ReLU and the net collapses to one straight line. Nonlinearity is what lets decision boundaries bend.

terms.hook: If they say this, modules hold the learnable parameters.

sittings.bodyEn: If loss does not drop, you may have forgotten zero_grad, or the learning rate is far too large or too small. CrossEntropyLoss wants class ids as long integers and raw logits — do not softmax first. Wrong device means model and data are not both on the same device. If evaluation numbers jump around, you forgot eval mode and no_grad, so dropout is still on. Use cuda on NVIDIA, mps on Apple silicon, cpu otherwise; for Project 5 fine-tuning prefer a CUDA GPU.

terms.hook: If they say this, match model and batch to device memory.

sittings.bodyEn: Batched attention-style matmul shape. Inner dims 64 must match. Outer dims 128 and 128 stay. Batch 8 rides along unchanged.
Five training lines from memory. Forward builds predictions. Loss scores them. Zero grad clears old slopes. Backward fills new ones. Step updates weights.
sittings.prompt: What is the order of one training step?
